text:
maria: Quick Q from today's tenant onboarding call — customer asked two things we should put in the SQ: 1) incident log retention and how long we keep searchable audit trail, and 2) delegated KMS access pattern + whether customer can rotate keys independently. Need a short blurb for the form.

devon: tl;dr we keep admin/audit logs 365 days by default. Enterprise customers can request extended retention up to 7 years (legal/archival) via contract addendum. :white_check_mark:

aj: for SIEM: we support streaming audit events to customer SIEM via secure webhook or syslog (TLS, mTLS). Customers can ingest events in near-real time — retention on their side is theirs, we retain copy for our retention window.

sre_oncall: important to call out what we redact before exporting: API keys, full JWTs, and any user-supplied secrets — we keep metadata, request IDs, timestamps, affected resource IDs. Example redaction rules are in the docs.

maria: can we include short KMS answer: they asked if they can bring their own key (BYOK) and rotate without our intervention.

devon: yes — we support envelope encryption with customer-managed CMKs (Cloud KMS / HSM). We hold only the wrapped data key. Customers can rotate their CMKs; after rotation new envelopes use the new CMK. We cannot unwrap customer CMKs or import private key material.

aj: add nuance: for Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments we provide HSM-backed option; for Hosted we support cloud KMS providers and a delegated-access pattern (read-only audit proofs signed by our key + customer CMK binding).

sec-bot: FYI: security playbook link https://redwood.example/internal/sec/playbooks/incidents#retention (access: eng + sec)

maria: customer also asked about ephemeral responder access for IR — can we issue time-limited investigator roles scoped to a tenant?

devon: yes, we have an "incident_investigator" role with scoped permissions (read-only audit, export logs, create snapshots). Token lifetime defaults to 1h, max 12h via Console > Access > Temporary roles. Example policy snippet we can paste in SQ: 
```
role: incident_investigator
permissions:
  - audit.logs.read
  - audit.snapshots.create
  - tenant.secrets.view? false
  - tenant.config.read
session_ttl: 3600
```

aj: also include how we authenticate temporary sessions: we issue short-lived JWTs via our OIDC service and record every session in audit stream (including subject, requester, justification).

maria: what about proof of logs (integrity) — customer wants to know if logs are tamper-evident for legal holds.

devon: we sign log batches server-side with an HMAC that we keep in a write-once audit store; for enterprise customers we can optionally register the hash chain with customer KM (BYOK) so they can verify integrity independently. We should phrase: "logs are cryptographically chained and can be verified against a customer-bound integrity key."

sre_oncall: operational note — exporting the full proof package requires an export job that includes signed manifest + zipped logs; we limit exports to approved roles and record export events.

aj: small caveat to call out: if customer rotates their CMK and asks us to re-wrap historical envelopes, we do not perform mass re-wrap automatically. We will provide a migration tool / guidance and can run a re-wrap job under a professional services engagement.

maria: please draft the two-paragraph SQ answer combining retention + KMS + IR ephemeral access + logs proof. Keep it vendor-friendly and not too deep. Also add one-line: contact sec-eng@redwood.com for PS quote.

devon: Will draft now, pushing to docs PR and will paste final here.

devon: DRAFT: "Redwood retains operational and audit logs for 365 days by default. For Enterprise agreements, retention can be extended up to seven years by contract. Audit events can be streamed to customer SIEMs in real time, and exports are available to authorized roles. Sensitive secrets (API keys, full tokens) are redacted before export; metadata, timestamps, request and resource IDs are retained for forensic analysis.

We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via envelope encryption. Redwood stores only wrapped data keys; customers retain control of their CMKs and can rotate them independently. For added integrity, audit logs are cryptographically chained; enterprise customers may bind the chain to a customer key for independent verification. Temporary investigator roles can be issued with short TTLs (default 1h) and all sessions and exports are fully recorded in the audit trail. For re-wrapping historical artifacts or bespoke key management workflows, please contact sec-eng@redwood.com for options and professional services."

maria: perfect — can you also include a 1-liner for the call notes: "If customer requires >7y retention or legal hold tooling, escalate to SalesOps for contract amendment; for re-wrap or HSM integration open a PS ticket."

aj: I'll add the SIEM export config pointers to the docs PR (webhook mTLS sample + syslog TLS sample).

maria: Action items: devon — open docs PR with the draft and add the PR link to the SQ response; aj — add SIEM config snippet; mre: escalate retention ask to SalesOps if customer marks >7y. I'll follow up with customer tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sre_oncall: leaving note: ensure on-call runbook references the investigator role and export audit steps (runbook ID: runbook/ir-exports).

sec-bot: Created ticket: SEC-7421 (owner: devon) — deadline EOD +2 for SQ draft and PR.

maria: thanks all, will paste finalized SQ reply to customer after PR merges.
